definitions.gloss: (spirits) cut with hot water; hot-water highball
definitions.explanation: An alcoholic drink, typically {焼酎|しょうちゅう} or whisky, diluted with hot water. Commonly drunk in winter to warm up. The base spirit is usually named: {焼酎|しょうちゅう}の{湯割|ゆわ}り.

examples.japanese: {焼酎|しょうちゅう}の{湯割|ゆわ}りを{一杯|いっぱい}ください。
examples.english: One shochu with hot water, please.

examples.japanese: {寒|さむ}い{夜|よる}は{湯割|ゆわ}りが{体|からだ}を{温|あたた}めてくれる。
examples.english: On a cold night, a hot-water highball warms you up.

examples.japanese: {父|ちち}は{毎晩|まいばん}{芋焼酎|いもじょうちゅう}を{湯割|ゆわ}りにして{飲|の}んでいる。
examples.english: My father drinks sweet-potato shochu cut with hot water every night.

notes:
Compound of {湯|ゆ} (hot water) + {割|わ}り (dilution). Contrasts with {水割|みずわ}り (cut with cold water) and ロック (on the rocks).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {焼酎|しょうちゅう}の{湯割|ゆわ}り: shochu cut with hot water
- {湯割|ゆわ}りで{飲|の}む: to drink it as a yuwari
- {湯割|ゆわ}りにする: to make it a yuwari

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {水割|みずわ}り: cut with cold water — same idea but cold
- {お{湯割|ゆわ}り}: polite form, used in restaurants/bars
- ロック: on the rocks — no water, just ice
